articles.title: Tech stocks rally after Nvidia board approves Jensen Huang's return as CEO
articles.summary: Major tech stocks rebounded across the board Monday, following Friday's steep sell-off when artificial intelligence stocks fell in the Nasdaq's worst week since 2020. Tech stocks remain rocky as investors remain nervous about the valuation of some AI companies and business models. Stocks of Big Tech companies and other stocks related to the AI trade also saw a lift Monday after the Nvidia news.

articles.title: Treasury yields jump as stock futures rebound, investors await New York Fed President Williams speech
articles.summary: Treasury yields rose on Monday, partially unwinding price action seen at the end of last week, as stock futures pointed to a strong rebound on Wall Street and investors look ahead to comments from John Williams of the New York Fed. The 2-year Treasury note yield, the most sensitive to short-term Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, was up more than 5 basis points at 4.67%.

articles.title: More Americans pay this Obama-era investment tax every year — how to avoid it
articles.summary: Every year, more Americans pay an extra tax levy on their investment gains — but there's still time to reduce or avoid that bill for 2026, experts say. Net investment income tax, or NIIT, is a 3.8% levy on investment income once earnings exceed $200,000 for single filers or $250,000 for married couples filing jointly.

articles.title: SpaceX sued by Oregon and Virginia over AI deepfake porn, Grok safety claims
articles.summary: Lawsuits against Elon Musk's SpaceX are stacking up, with Virginia and Oregon becoming the first states to sue the company over issues with its Grok AI image generator. The complaints also allege that SpaceX has falsely represented its AI apps and social network (Grok and X) as generally safe, which the states see as a violation of Virginia's Consumer Protection Act or Oregon's Unlawful Trade Practices Act.

articles.summary: stocks looks set to help major markets crawl away from correction territory. Technology stocks sank in overnight trading, with SK Hynix among the biggest losers, weighing on South Korea's Kospi. Meanwhile, chip stocks are also in the green, rebounding from last week's sell-off.

articles.title: French biotech rejects short seller’s cancer-risk claims after shares plunge 17%
articles.summary: French biotech Abivax's stock has partially recovered after the company responded to short seller Scorpion Capital accusing it of serious scientific and safety shortcomings in its experimental inflammatory bowel disease drug, obefazimod. After the closing bell, Abivax said Scorpion's report contained "numerous factually inaccurate and misleading statements, assumptions, and conclusions." Shares rose 10% in Monday morning trading.

articles.title: Investors gives a thumbs down to Tata Steel-APL Apollo $1.67 billion deal, plunging shares
articles.summary: The acquisition will boost Tata Steel's downstream integration to around 53% from 35%, the company said in a stock exchange filing. Investors reacted negatively to the deal, with shares of Tata Steel sliding over 9% on Monday, while APL Apollo's stock crashed more than 19%. While the deal is likely to be positive in the long term, the complex structure and lack of clarity have rattled investors, Deven Choksey, founder and managing director of wealth management firm DRChoksey FinServ, told CNBC.
